How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
IP: 192.120.45.67
API name: get information of an interface
Parameter_fabricName: Network1
Parameter_nodeId: 12
Parameter_podId: 10
Parameter_interfaceType: Ethernet
Parameter_infoType: Speed

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Send a GET request to retrieve specified information for an interface from a network telemetry API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL endpoint to send the GET request to. This should include the base path without query parameters, e.g., 'https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo'.

params.description: The query parameters for the request.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit nodes pertaining to.

nodeId.description: The node identifier to limit results pertaining to.

podId.description: The pod identifier to limit results pertaining to.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit results pertaining to.

infoType.description: The type of information requested for the interface.

message.content:
Below is the exact REST‑style request you would send to the Cisco Nexus Dashboard API to fetch the **Speed** information for an Ethernet interface on node 12 in pod 10 of fabric “Network1”.

---

## 1️⃣ Full URL (with query string)

```
https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=Ethernet&infoType=Speed
```

> *The base path (`/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo`) is the same as the one used in the `requests_get` function definition.*

---

## 2️⃣ Example `curl` command

```bash
curl -k \
     -H "Accept: application/json" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN>" \
     "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=Ethernet&infoType=Speed"
```

*Replace `<YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN>` with the bearer token you obtain from the Nexus Dashboard OAuth flow.*

---

## 3️⃣ Using the provided `functions.requests_get` wrapper

If you’re calling this from a Python script that has the `functions` namespace available, you can invoke it like this:

```python
from functions import requests_get

response = requests_get({
    "url": "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo",
    "params": {
        "fabricName": "Network1",
        "nodeId": 12,
        "podId": 10,
        "interfaceType": "Ethernet",
        "infoType": "Speed"
    }
})

print(response)   # <-- will contain the JSON payload returned by the API
```

> **Note:**  
> *The wrapper will automatically handle the HTTP GET request and return the parsed JSON (or raw response) as defined by the `any` return type.*

---

### Quick checklist before sending the request

| Item | What to do |
|------|------------|
| **Base URL** | `https://192.120.45.67` |
| **Endpoint** | `/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo` |
| **Query params** | `fabricName=Network1`, `nodeId=12`, `podId=10`, `interfaceType=Ethernet`, `infoType=Speed` |
| **HTTP method** | `GET` |
| **Headers** | `Accept: application/json`, `Authorization: Bearer <token>` |
| **SSL** | Use `-k` in curl or set `verify=False` in Python if you’re using self‑signed certs. |

Once you hit the endpoint, you should receive a JSON payload similar to:

```json
{
  "fabricName": "Network1",
  "nodeId": 12,
  "podId": 10,
  "interfaceType": "Ethernet",
  "infoType": "Speed",
  "speedMbps": 1000
}
```

(Actual field names may vary depending on the API version.)

Happy querying!
